title: Site transport and integral realization of clopen system comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X	o Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, without assuming $Y$ separated over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions covering $X$, with $g_i=g\circ j_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty components and the empty cover of $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

Fix compactifications $c=(a,p)$, $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $ho_{i,A}:r_{i,A}G_{g,A}\cong G_{g_i,A}$ be the counit-normalized comparison on actual derived strict etale coefficient systems [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison]; the categories, evaluations and etale/pro-etale system comparison are those of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Write $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the comparison morphism, and use $
u_{T,A}^*$ and $R
u_{T,A,*}$ on systems. There is an exact-derived restriction square $r_{i,A}
u_{X,A}^*\cong
u_{X_i,A}^*r_{i,A}$ induced by the canonical underlying sheaf square and compatible with strict transitions. Whiskering $ho_{i,A}$ gives an isomorphism
$$r_{i,A}
u_{X,A}^*G_{g,A}R
u_{Y,A,*}\cong

u_{X_i,A}^*G_{g_i,A}R
u_{Y,A,*}.$$
On bounded constructible inputs its finite evaluations equal the finite pro-etale counit-normalized comparisons of [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison], through the canonical open-extension site comparison and compactification adjunctions.

For integral $L\in D^b_c(Y,O)$, use the ACTUAL derived reduction system $\mathcal R_YL$, the system exceptional functor $\mathcal T_g=
u_{X,A}^*G_{g,A}R
u_{Y,A,*}\mathcal R_Y$, and the exact scalar-forgetting functor $DU_X$ to strict towers of completed-$O$ modules, all as in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The preceding map gives a natural isomorphism of derived strict systems $r_{i,A}\mathcal T_gL\cong\mathcal T_{g_i}L$. Restriction commutes with $DU$, finite reduction and the actual total derived inverse-limit functor on strict towers [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its image under $R\lim\circ DU$ is a natural isomorphism
$$Lj_i^*Rg_O^!L\xrightarrow{\sim}R(g_i)_O^!L.$$
Here $Lj_i^*$ is the integral completed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], canonically identified on derived-complete constructible complexes with component restriction. The identification commutes with reduction and the total-limit realization, using $K\cong R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes_O^LA_n)$ for derived-complete $K$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. Both $\mathcal T$ functors use the displayed common-proper-part compactifications. This is the image of an actual system isomorphism on objects and morphisms, with its inverse; it does not assert the existence of a lift of an arbitrary diagram in the ordinary derived category.

proof.text:
Write $N_T=
u_T^*$. For each $n$, the canonical pullback square in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], inverted, gives $q_{i,n}:r_iN_X\cong N_{X_i}r_i$. Regard it as a map of constant-$A_n$ modules by transporting the action along the constant-section identifications. Naturality applied to multiplication by each scalar makes it linear; applied to a transition $M_{n+1}	o\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ it gives the strict-system square, since both comparison maps are induced by the same underlying inverse-image square and leave scalar actions unchanged. Thus $(q_{i,n})_n$ is a natural isomorphism on abelian strict systems, not independently chosen maps of derived evaluations. Both inverse images and restriction are exact; the system functors and their exactness are as in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Apply the square termwise to complexes. It preserves differentials and chain homotopies by naturality, and quasi-isomorphisms by exactness. The transformation and its inverse descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], giving $q_{i,A}:r_{i,A}
u_{X,A}^*\cong
u_{X_i,A}^*r_{i,A}$ with the specified strict transitions.

proof.text:
For $N\in D(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{proet}}))$ put $H=R
u_{Y,A,*}N$. Define
$$\sigma_{i,N}=
u_{X_i,A}^*(ho_{i,A,H})\circ q_{i,A,G_{g,A}H}.$$
Here $ho_{i,A}$ is the actual natural system isomorphism of [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison]. Its inverse, followed by $q^{-1}$ in the reverse order, is an inverse for $\sigma$. Naturality is composition of the two naturality squares. The evaluation comparisons in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] identify $e_nR
u_{Y,A,*}N$ with $R
u_{Y,*}e_nN$ and $e_n
u_{X,A}^*$ with $
u_X^*e_n$. The same lemma identifies the comparison units and counits, and the clopen comparison node identifies $e_nho_{i,A}$ with the ordinary etale counit-normalized map. Consequently $e_n\sigma_i$ is precisely its whiskering by $R
u_{Y,*}$ and $
u_{X_i}^*$, with $q_{i,n}$ on its source. All these assertions concern evaluations of the already constructed system arrow.

proof.text: We check the open-extension normalization needed to identify that evaluated arrow. At level $n$, write $e_i=j_{i,!}^{et}$, $d_i=j_{i,!}^{pro}$ and $c_i:N_Xe_i\cong d_iN_{X_i}$. The unit-normalized comparison of [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization] identifies these specified maps and their adjunctions. In the clopen decomposition zero insertion is $j_{i,!}$, with identity after restriction to $X_i$, by [lem-pur-clopen-common-compact-support]; the etale system version and its evaluated adjunction maps are in [lem-pur-clopen-strict-system-support]. Thus the insertion counit is preserved by this site comparison: its restriction to $X_i$ is the identity on both sides, and on every other component it is zero. The clopen equivalence [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] detects this equality. The open compositors for $a\circ j_i$ are likewise identified: their restriction to the source component is the identity, and they are zero off that component. Applying the same proper direct image $Rp_*$ gives the compact-support compositor $b_i$. In the canonical proper-and-open site comparison of [lem-amb-compact-support-site-comparison-open], the proper factor is the SAME for $c$ and $c_i$; naturality of this factor with respect to the open compositor therefore identifies the two $b_i$ maps. This is equality of the specified maps, not just isomorphism of their endpoints.

source.place: Retained old step 8: canonical open-extension, insertion-counit and common-proper-part compatibility

proof.text:
For bounded constructible finite input $L_n$, use the transported bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for $g$ and $g_i$. Their hypotheses hold: [lem-pur-clopen-common-compact-support] supplies a common compactification with Noetherian schemes and finite-dimensional proper source, without requiring $Y$ separated. These are the transported adjunctions defining the finite functors in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Apply those Hom bijections to the evaluated etale counit equation for $\rho_{i,A}$. Step 3 identifies its $b_i$ and insertion-counit terms with their pro-etale terms; the exceptional counit is the transpose of the identity under the same transported Hom bijection. Hence the evaluated $\sigma$ satisfies exactly
$$\varepsilon_{g_i,L_n}F_{g_i}(e_n\sigma_{i,L_n})=\varepsilon_{g,L_n}F_g(c^{ins}_{i,G_gL_n})b_{i,r_iG_gL_n}^{-1}.$$
The uniqueness assertion in [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison] now identifies it with $\rho_{i,n}$. We use uniqueness on this bounded constructible domain; no adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale inputs and no faithfulness of derived evaluations is needed.

source.place: Retained old step 8: transpose the actual counit equation on the bounded constructible domain

proof.text: For integral $L$, precompose $\sigma_i$ with the actual reduction functor $\mathcal R_Y$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The result $s_{i,L}:r_{i,A}\mathcal T_gL\cong\mathcal T_{g_i}L$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of strict systems, natural in integral derived morphisms. On complexes, restriction followed by $DU_X$ and $DU_{X_i}$ followed by system restriction have the same underlying sheaves, differentials and transitions. Their completed-ring actions agree because the coefficient identifications preserve every projection to $A_n$ [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing]. The same equality holds on strict system maps. Exactness permits descent to the derived categories, as in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus $DU(s_i)$ is an actual isomorphism of derived strict completed-coefficient towers. Finite reduction commutes with restriction by [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition], retaining its quotient transitions; we do not try to recover $s_i$ from the collection of its finite evaluations.

source.place: Retained old step 9: apply actual reduction and scalar forgetting

proof.text: Restriction commutes with the TOTAL derived inverse-limit functor, with the required map action. Indeed the exact clopen equivalence of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] extends levelwise to strict towers, with exact zero insertion $E_i$ left adjoint to restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], restriction carries a K-injective tower resolution $C\to J$ to a K-injective resolution of $r_iC$. Ordinary inverse limits commute with restriction: under the product equivalence they are componentwise limits, with the same compatible families and projections. Hence the formula of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives $r_iR\lim C=r_i\lim J\cong\lim r_iJ=R\lim r_iC$. These comparisons commute with maps of resolutions and descend naturally; applying them to the identity and composition gives the same identities, since the comparisons before localization do so. This proves commutation for the total derived functor, rather than only for objects specified by a Roos triangle. Finite reduction compatibility is the one already supplied in Step 5.

Apply $R\lim$ to $DU(s_{i,L})$ and use Step 6. The defining formula $Rg_O^!=R\lim\circ DU_X\circ\mathcal T_g$ in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with $c=(a,p)$ and $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ throughout, yields a natural isomorphism $\tau_{i,L}:r_iRg_O^!L\cong R(g_i)_O^!L$. Put $K=Rg_O^!L$, which belongs to the integral constructible category by that definition's stipulated constructible operation. The canonical natural isomorphism $\kappa_K:r_iK\to Lj_i^*K$ of [lem-pur-open-completed-restriction-identification] identifies the ACTUAL completed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with component restriction. Therefore the claimed arrow is $\tau_{i,L}\circ\kappa_K^{-1}$. That node identifies the strict quotient-tower comparison, augmentations, projections and positive reductions, so this is also the asserted compatibility with $K\cong R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes_O^LA_n)$. In particular we use its canonical natural reconstruction comparison, not a non-unique isomorphism supplied merely by the existence of a triangle in the definition of derived completeness.

source.place: Retained old step 9: actual integral realization and canonical completed-pullback identification

proof.text: Every comparison above has an inverse before or after application of an actual functor. Sending its two inverse equations through $DU$ and $R\lim$ gives the two inverse equations integrally; naturality follows by applying these functors to the system naturality square. If $X_i$ is empty, the clopen module and system factors are zero, so every displayed map on that factor is the unique zero-to-zero map. If $I$ is empty, the cover condition forces $X=\varnothing$ and there is no component assertion. These are the zero-category conventions of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition, lem-pur-clopen-strict-system-support]. The proof constructs one system isomorphism with its inverse and then its functorial image; it never lifts an arbitrary diagram of ordinary derived objects.

The two added stmt_deps (site-comparison-morphism, derived-complete-integral-detailed) are both used by the statement. The union of the step uses equals proof_deps, every cited id exists and none is merged, and there is no cycle. I compared the proof with Q121's retained old steps 8-9 (report lines 140-156): steps 1-4 expand old step 8 and steps 5-7 expand old step 9, with nothing dropped. Two vague sentences of the old text are now real arguments: the K-injective argument for the total limit (Stacks 08BJ derived.tex:9857 and 0941 sites-cohomology.tex:5067, both checked) and the canonical kappa node for the completed pullback. Every cited statement says what each step takes from it. Step 1: linearity follows because nu^* on modules is defined by applying it to the scalar endomorphisms. Step 3: the compositor equalities hold because maps out of an extension by zero are determined on the open, where both sides are unit-normalized; J is explicitly the open-then-proper composite, and c and c_i share p. Step 4: the thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class hypotheses (finite type, separated g and g_i, dim of the compactification bounded by d, etale-origin source) are supplied by the common-compact-support node; uniqueness is applied to a finite natural transformation. Step 6: zero insertion is an exact left adjoint of restriction on towers. Step 7: ell is invertible on X, K lies in the integral D^b_c by the definition's typing clause, and the pur-integral Lj^* is the same operation as the one in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. Small cases checked: Y+Y with the fold map, a single component, empty components, the empty cover and n=1. A non-separated Y is retained. No duplicate exists among the clopen site/Roos/tower/scalar-descent nodes. I accept the eight declared generic tool uses. No SGA source is used.
